sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: No supplied candidate defines the required per-craft ship-to-craft applicability path for determining which individual rescue boats or lifeboats are released, nor does any candidate establish the required lifeboat-to-survival-craft identity alignment; the available releasedRescueBoatOrLifeboat boolean would incorrectly support global ship-level application.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS

Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Fix: COMPLETE dependency relationship(s) absent from candidate: hasDistressAlertDevice, hasLifeboat, hasOtherSurvivalCraft, hasRequiredRescueBoatOrLifeboat
Semantic validator feedback: Add every relationship declared by the COMPLETE dependency contract: nltl:hasDistressAlertDevice on the declared lifeboat owner, nltl:hasLifeboat and nltl:hasRequiredRescueBoatOrLifeboat on the ship, and nltl:hasOtherSurvivalCraft on the ship, while retaining nltl:hasSurvivalCraft and the three survival-craft device paths on their declared owners. The current candidate omits four mandatory relationship terms and therefore does not faithfully encode the required craft-to-device and ship-to-craft paths.

Preserve the completed relationship coverage from the prior instruction, but repair the semantics: do not require shipOperatesInLowAirTemperature=true or releasedRescueBoatOrLifeboat=true with sh:hasValue, since the requirement is conditional and these inputs determine applicability. Encode the three minimum device requirements only when low-temperature applicability and release applicability hold; missing applicability evidence must not pass. Scope those checks to every applicable released rescue boat/lifeboat, not every survival craft, and ensure the lifeboat path carries all three required device relationships rather than only hasDistressAlertDevice. Avoid unconditional minCount existence constraints for craft relationships unless independently required; retain the declared relationship paths without turning alternatives or inventory categories into mandatory conjunctive facts.

Repair the applicability ownership and coverage while preserving the completed relationship set. The canonical requiredOwner for releasedRescueBoatOrLifeboat is ship, so do not place that property on each lifeboat; request/use the canonical cross-owner ship-to-craft applicability path and activate the matcher for that missing path. Apply the conditional check to every released lifeboat/rescue-boat reached through both declared ship relationships, including hasLifeboat, not only hasRequiredRescueBoatOrLifeboat. Missing low-temperature or release applicability evidence must fail rather than bypass the query. Enforce exactly the three required device relationships: ship-to-shore distress alert, location signal, and on-scene communication. Retain hasDistressAlertDevice as the declared lifeboat relationship, but do not make it an additional fourth mandatory device or overconstrain the requirement.

Preserve the completed relationship coverage and prior applicability instructions, but do not freeze this graph. The candidate still lacks the canonical ship-to-craft applicability path needed to determine which individual rescue boats/lifeboats are released; the ship-level releasedRescueBoatOrLifeboat boolean is incorrectly applied globally to every craft reached by the union path. Locate and use that canonical cross-owner path, and ensure missing applicability evidence fails. Also align the checked craft with the declared owner/path structure: the query reaches lifeboats via hasLifeboat or hasRequiredRescueBoatOrLifeboat but checks survivalCraftHas* predicates without a declared lifeboat-to-survivalCraft relationship or guaranteed survivalCraft identity, so the three device requirements can target the wrong entity. Retain all declared relationships, including hasDistressAlertDevice on lifeboat, without making it an additional fourth device requirement; enforce the three required device relationships on each applicable released rescue boat/lifeboat.
